memoryText: But I do not account my life of any value nor as precious to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the gospel of the grace of God.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Acts 20:24 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Paul says this to the Ephesian elders on the beach at Miletus, knowing that he is going to Jerusalem and that chains and afflictions await.

“I do not account my life of any value nor as precious to myself.” Paul is not careless about his life. He knows its worth, but he does not hold it as the highest good. For him, life is a trust, to be spent for something greater.

“If only I may finish my course.” He pictures his life as a race to finish. A course has a beginning and an end, and the goal is to complete it. In his last letter, Paul writes that he has fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.

“And the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus.” The task is not Paul’s invention. It is received, given by the Lord Jesus himself. Each of us also receives a calling.

“To testify to the gospel of the grace of God.” This is the center of Paul’s ministry. Not his own cleverness, but the good news of grace: that sinners are saved freely by God’s favor in Christ.

When you are afraid of the cost of faithfulness, say this verse. The goal is not to protect our lives but to finish the course and testify to the grace of God.
weekInReview: This week you saw Paul on the road: a full Jerusalem Council behind him and the ministry in Ephesus finished. You read his tender farewell to the Ephesian elders, with its charge to shepherd the church of God, which he obtained with his own blood. Three psalms sang the mission: Psalm 96, declare his glory among the nations; Psalm 98, all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God; and Psalm 100, enter his gates with thanksgiving. Then Paul went up to Jerusalem, knowing what awaited him. You watched him seized in the temple, retell his conversion on the steps, stand before the council and Felix, and speak of the hope of the resurrection. The Lord told him, “Take courage… you must testify also in Rome.”
reflectionQuestions: Paul said he did not count his life as precious if only he could finish his course. What is one thing in your life that you are holding too tightly, and what would it look like to hold it more loosely for the sake of Christ?
Paul told the elders to care for the church “which he obtained with his own blood.” How does that change the way you think about your own church and its people?
Felix heard the truth, was alarmed, and put it off. Is there a truth God is pressing on you that you’ve been postponing? What is one step you can take today?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for the church he bought with his blood.
Ask him to help you finish your course.
